failure_summary.description: Agents consistently over-specify answers by extracting long descriptive phrases, categories, or full clauses instead of the precise, minimal core entity requested by short/fragment questions.

patch.reasoning: All three failures involve agents returning verbose descriptive phrases, categories, or full biographical clauses ('president of Vietnam from 1997 to 2006', 'Nordic countries', 'Speech balloon') when the gold answers require a single, minimal core entity ('Vietnam', 'Sweden', 'a balloon'). The existing conciseness rules are insufficiently enforced for fragmentary or keyword-only queries. A targeted rule enforcing minimal entity extraction and stripping of non-essential modifiers will correct this systematic over-specification.

edits.content: - **Minimal Entity Enforcement**: For short, fragmentary, or keyword-only questions, extract only the single core entity or exact term. Strip all descriptive clauses, temporal markers, titles, and categories. If the context provides a long phrase, reduce it to the precise noun requested. Never output multi-word descriptions unless they form a fixed proper name.
